Dear Lower GI urgent suspected cancer team,

Re: Synthetic Given 086 Synthetic Family 086, DOB 1976-03-06, NHS SYN-NHS-000086

I am writing to refer this 50-year-old woman under the 2WW lower GI pathway. She first attended my colleague six weeks ago complaining of intermittent bright red rectal bleeding and a noticeable change in her bowel habit -- she has gone from one formed stool every other day to three to four loose stools per day. She reports lower abdominal cramping that is relieved by defaecation.

A faecal immunochemical test was sent on 2026-05-08. The pathology report annotates the result as "FIT pos" (numeric value 198 ug Hb/g, well above the local 10 ug/g referral threshold). She has had no previous FIT testing -- I would like to clarify, for the record, that this was not a FIT requested in a previous episode that has now come back; this is the index test for this presentation. On digital rectal examination there are no haemorrhoids and no rectal mass. Bloods are enclosed and show borderline iron-deficient indices.

Past medical and family history: well-controlled essential hypertension (amlodipine 5mg OD), no family history of bowel cancer, no inflammatory bowel disease. She is a non-smoker. BMI 26.

She is fit for day-case investigation, has capacity to consent, and is aware that this is a suspected cancer referral. I have given safety-net advice in the meantime.

Kind regards,
Dr Synthetic GP 06
